piece.title: String Quartet in E-flat major
piece.why: Fanny Hensel's Romanza: Violin I states the theme, the viola echoes a phrase, then the cello restates the theme in its high tenor register under a Violin I countermelody.

roster.label: Church brass: 2 trumpets (one beginner), horn, euphonium

plan.summary: Trumpet 1 plays the tune all the way through. It takes the Violin 1 melody in bars 1–12, at written pitch or an octave lower depending on the phrase so it stays in range and above the harmony, then the cello's return of the theme in bars 13–16. The euphonium always plays whatever line is lowest in the strings, mostly the cello but Violin 2 or viola in a few bars. The horn plays the soft viola harmony. In the last phrase the horn moves to Violin 1's countermelody and the beginner trumpet adds Violin 2's harmony, before both drop out for the final two bars so the theme and bass end clearly.

assignments.reason: Main tune, played an octave lower so the high notes fit the trumpet.
The tune dips low here, so the trumpet plays it at written pitch to stay above the viola harmony. [checker moved this line -1 octave(s) to fit the range]
Back down an octave where the tune climbs high, so it stays in the trumpet's range.
Written pitch, so the tune stays above the viola when it dips and fits the low D4/Eb4 in bars 9–10. [checker: mm. 7-8 at -1 octave(s) to fit the range]
Written pitch, so the tune stays above the viola when it dips and fits the low D4/Eb4 in bars 9–10. [checker: mm. 9-10 at +0 octave(s) to fit the range]
The tune climbs to Ab5 here, so the trumpet goes down an octave to stay in range.
The cello brings back the theme, and Trumpet 1 keeps the tune in one voice.
Violin 2's low G3 is the lowest note in bar 1, so the euphonium plays it as the bass.
The viola is the lowest line in this bar. Played an octave lower, it fits the euphonium and stays at the bottom.
Cello bass line at written pitch, including the long held G2 pedal.
This bar dips to E2, below the euphonium's range, so it is played an octave higher.
Descending walking bass at written pitch.
The viola is the lowest line from the cadence onward (held G3, then A3 and D3), so the euphonium follows it to stay at the bottom.
Viola inner harmony. The horn's round sound blends behind the tune.
The cello's rising figure (up to G4), which the euphonium can't reach. It fits the horn exactly.
Viola inner harmony. It fits the horn's range completely, and the horn's soft sound sits behind the trumpet tune.
The cello's rise to G4 at the cadence, which is too high for the euphonium. The horn takes it at written pitch.
Violin 1's countermelody against the returning theme, an octave lower to fit the horn.
An easy entry for the beginner: the cello's repeated B3, well within range.
Two held F4s at written pitch, an easy part for the beginner.
Violin 2 harmony, an octave lower to fit the beginner's range.

dropped.reason: Repeated-note and chord filler that sits above the tune. The only free player is the beginner trumpet, which would cover the tune and can't reach E5. The horn and euphonium already cover the harmony.
It is too high for the beginner at written pitch, and an octave lower it would sink under the theme.
Countermelody that goes up to Bb5. The horn could only play it an octave lower, which would put it under the theme at the cadence, so the ending is left to the theme and bass.
